title: The count comes down as a coefficient
spoken: The entropy change is k B times the logarithm of W, which is n times k B times the logarithm of f.
explanation: Boltzmann's principle turns the probability into an entropy difference. The logarithm of f to the n is n times the logarithm of f, so the number of independent points becomes the coefficient, and that coefficient is what section 6 compares with the radiation's entropy.
assumptions: n points move independently of one another, each equally likely to be anywhere in the volume V₀.
The chosen part V is a fraction f = V/V₀ of that volume.
Boltzmann's principle, as the paper states it: an entropy difference is Boltzmann's constant times the logarithm of a relative probability.
These are modern teaching equations in SI notation, not a transcription of the printed paper. The paper writes R/N for Boltzmann's constant.

notes.explanation: Boltzmann's principle, the name the paper gives it.

notes.title: Logarithm of the fraction
notes.explanation: Negative when f is less than one, so confining the points lowers their entropy.

notes.title: Logarithm of the probability
notes.explanation: Entropy differences go as the logarithm of relative probability.

notes.title: Boltzmann's principle
notes.explanation: The entropy difference from the probability of the configuration.

notes.title: n times Boltzmann's constant times ln f
notes.explanation: The logarithm of f to the n is n times the logarithm of f.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: The entropy change is proportional to the number of independent points.

notes.title: Boltzmann's constant
notes.explanation: Turns the logarithm of a probability into an entropy; R over N in the paper.

notes.title: Boltzmann's constant
notes.explanation: Turns the logarithm of a probability into an entropy; R over N in the paper.

notes.title: Entropy change of the points
notes.explanation: The entropy with the points confined minus the entropy with them free: a difference, not an absolute entropy.

notes.title: Number of independent points
notes.explanation: How many points move independently of one another.

notes.title: Fraction of the volume
notes.explanation: The share of the volume the points must all be in, V over V₀; between 0 and 1.

notes.title: Probability of the configuration
notes.explanation: The chance that, at one instant, all n points are in the chosen part of the volume.
